consent.text: Steelcase and Logitech are running The Hybrid Equation together. This assessment asks about your meeting spaces, technology and habits. Your answers, your readiness score and the areas where your organisation scores lowest will be shared with Steelcase and Logitech so we can send you your results and relevant follow-up about hybrid meetings, in line with the PDPA and other applicable privacy rules. We also use combined, anonymised results to describe overall trends.

profileQuestions.label: How many people work at your primary office or campus?
Which market are you based in?

areas.name: Spaces
areas.blurb: Rooms where everyone faces the camera and display help remote people feel present, not like observers.

areas.name: Technology
areas.blurb: Clear audio, framing cameras, and one-touch starts remove the most common hybrid meeting friction.

areas.name: Meeting equity
areas.blurb: Shared content and inclusive room setups let remote colleagues contribute on equal footing, not just listen.

areas.name: People and habits
areas.blurb: Simple shared habits and leader role-modelling make every hybrid call more inclusive and consistent.

areas.name: Support and planning
areas.blurb: Clear cross-functional ownership and room-use data turn one-off fixes into steady improvement.

scoredQuestions.text: When you book a meeting room for a hybrid call, how often does it actually work well for it?
How are your meeting rooms set up?

options.text: Designed around the camera and screen, so everyone faces both
Mostly standard tables, with some rooms adapted
Standard boardroom tables with a screen at one end

scoredQuestions.text: Do you have the right mix of room sizes for how people meet today?

options.text: Yes, from focus booths to large rooms
Mostly, but small rooms are always full

scoredQuestions.text: Can remote participants clearly hear everyone in the room?

options.text: Always, even people at the far end
Often people need to repeat themselves

scoredQuestions.text: Can remote participants clearly see everyone in the room, not just the person nearest the camera?

options.text: Yes, the camera frames speakers automatically

scoredQuestions.text: How long does it take to start a hybrid meeting?

options.text: We often need IT to help

scoredQuestions.text: Can remote participants see and contribute to whiteboards or shared content?

options.text: Yes, easily and in real time
With a workaround, like taking photos

scoredQuestions.text: How often do remote participants get talked over or forgotten?
Do people prefer to join from their desk rather than walk into the meeting room?
Do your teams have shared ways of running hybrid meetings (e.g. one person checks the chat, everyone joins on time)?

options.text: Informally, it depends on the host

scoredQuestions.text: How confident are people using the meeting room technology without help?

options.text: Only a few people know how

scoredQuestions.text: Do leaders run hybrid meetings in a way that includes remote participants?
Does someone own the hybrid meeting experience in your organisation?

options.text: Yes, a named owner across facilities, IT and HR

scoredQuestions.text: Do you know how your meeting rooms are actually used (booked vs. used, room fit, problems)?

options.text: Yes, we track and act on it

scoredQuestions.text: Do you have a plan to improve hybrid meetings in the next 12 months?

bands.label: Getting started
bands.headline: You're at [X]%. Hybrid meetings are likely costing your teams time and energy.
bands.body: You're not alone: many workplaces added cameras without rethinking the room. The good news is that a few targeted changes make a visible difference fast.

bands.label: Making progress
bands.headline: You're at [X]%. The foundations are there, but remote colleagues are still missing out.
bands.body: Your teams can meet, but not yet as equals. Closing the gaps below is where you'll see the biggest jump in meeting quality.

bands.label: Nearly there
bands.headline: You're at [X]%. You're ahead of many, with a few gaps holding you back.
bands.body: Small fixes in your weakest area could make hybrid meetings feel effortless for everyone.

bands.label: Hybrid ready
bands.headline: You're at [X]%. Your hybrid meetings are working well.
bands.body: Keep it that way as teams and technology change. See how others are taking the next step.

spaces.headline: Your rooms weren't built for the screen
spaces.tip: Rooms where everyone faces the camera and display help remote people feel present, not like observers.

technology.headline: People can't always see or hear each other
technology.tip: Clear audio and cameras that frame whoever is speaking remove the most common hybrid frustrations.

equity.headline: Remote colleagues are on the sidelines
equity.tip: Shared whiteboards and content everyone can reach let remote people contribute, not just listen.

people.headline: Good hybrid meetings depend on who's hosting
people.tip: Simple shared habits, like one person watching the chat, make every meeting more inclusive.

support.headline: No one owns the hybrid experience
support.tip: A named owner and basic room-use data turn one-off fixes into steady improvement.
